subject: dwarfBlacksmith
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf blacksmith at an anvil.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.

spec.name: Dwarf Blacksmith at the Anvil
spec.description: A stocky Warcraft-style dwarf smith with braided red beard, plate pauldrons and leather apron, hammer raised over a glowing anvil beside a small forge.
spec.layout: The dwarf is about 1.35 m tall (huge Warcraft proportions: broad shoulders, big hands and boots, short legs, big head), standing at x=0, z=-0.15, facing +Z. In front of him (+Z) stands a heavy iron anvil on a log stump, centred at z=0.45. His right arm (model -X) is raised holding a big hammer above the anvil; his left arm (+X) holds tongs with a glowing bar on the anvil. A small stone forge with glowing coals sits behind-left (x=0.65, z=-0.45). Chunky, faceted, bold shapes; oversized pauldrons with rivets and spikes, braided beard with metal rings, saturated warm palette with glowing orange accents. Everything is flat colours and small seated detail parts.

parts.builds: Legs with boots (wide cuffed leather boots with gold buckles, cloth trousers), hips, belt with big gold buckle and hanging tools (pouch, small hammer), leather apron with stitched trim and soot stains, barrel torso with cloth shirt, and the neck. Uses the legs/hips/chest/neck joints. Boots must touch y=0 and be big and chunky.
parts.attaches: Shoulder mounts shoulderR/shoulderL for arms and pauldrons; neck mount for the head.

parts.builds: Big square characterful head: heavy brow ridge, big bulbous nose, deep-set eyes with white and dark pupils and bushy brows, ears, a separate upper skull and lower jaw (jaw joint), mouth hidden behind the beard. Huge braided red beard flowing down the chest in two braids with gold rings and tips, layered overlapping blades from beardLight to beard, moustache with curled ends, red hair with a topknot, and a small plate helmet band with a gold rune stud across the forehead.
parts.attaches: Sits on the neck mount; beard drapes over chest front without covering the belt.

parts.builds: Both arms and gear: oversized plate pauldrons with rivets, gold trim and spikes; leather bracers; muscular skin forearms with hair; big gloved hands. Right arm (-X) raised, gripping the hammer handle at handR; left arm (+X) forward holding long tongs gripping a glowing bar at handL. The hammer: wooden haft with leather wrap, big iron head with gold bands and a rune; head glows faintly at the striking face.
parts.attaches: Roots at shoulderR/shoulderL on the chest joint; hands reach handR and handL.

parts.builds: Heavy iron anvil (horn, face, waist, base feet) with a bright steel face, gold maker's mark, on a thick log stump with bark rings, axe marks and iron bands. A glowing orange-yellow bar on the face with a few spark particles (small hotYellow and ember cubes) floating above. Static, no joints.
parts.attaches: Top surface at anvilTop where the glowing bar lies for the tongs and hammer.

parts.builds: Small chunky stone forge behind-left: stacked rough stone blocks forming a hearth with a chimney hood, glowing coal bed (ember and hotYellow faceted lumps), iron grate, leather bellows with wooden handles, a bucket of water, and a rack with tongs and chisels on the wall side. Also a few small flame shapes in ember/hotYellow. Static, no joints.
parts.attaches: Centred on forgeCenter; stands on the floor beside the dwarf, not touching his arms.

I'll simplify by setting bone explicitly to J.hips for every part, since hips is the root joint and gives deterministic placement using the provided `at` coordinates. I'll also need to locally declare a minimal Ctx type for the function signature rather than relying on an import that may not exist.

Now I'm sketching the actual geometry: a bounding box roughly x±0.35, z 0.1–0.95, y 0–0.95, with the anvil top sitting around y=0.78 centered near z=0.45. The stump is a cylinder of radius 0.3 (spanning z 0.15–0.75, x ±0.3) reaching up to y=0.42, and the anvil body sits on top with height 0.36 to reach y=0.78, oriented with its long axis along X so the horn extends toward +X while the dwarf faces +Z. I'm leaving room above for floating spark particles near y=0.95.

Now I'm detailing the stump's bark texture with low-poly ridge plates in a darker wood tone, thin lighter rings at the cut top where visible past the anvil, iron bands with rivets wrapped around the stump, small angled axe-mark gouges, and flared root wedges at the base.

Writing part definitions...

Still working out the geometry...

I'll build a custom frustum geometry function generating 8 vertices and indexed triangles for the tapered shapes, then start laying out the anvil's feet and stump proportions from y=0.42 to 0.78.

Continuing the waist into a widening body frustum, then a steel face plate box at the top, keeping to a limited six-colour palette with a brighter steel tone for the plate. Now starting on a horn piece extending from the +X side.

Refining horn geometry...

Now I'm working out the heel/tail block on the opposite side, sizing a small box projection flush with the face plate to hold the hardy and pritchel holes, positioning it around x -0.23 to -0.30 at the anvil's top height.

I'm adding the hardy hole as a small dark square cutout and the pritchel hole as a round dark cylinder, both embedded in the face plate near the heel, then positioning the heated bar lying across the face so it extends toward the tongs grip point.

Working out the bar's exact position and rotation now — calculating the yaw angle so it angles correctly toward the handle, then setting up a glow effect with a hot yellow core and ember-colored outer edge for the heated metal.

I'm layering an inner hot core and outer ember box, both glowing, with the color cooling toward one end and brightening to yellow at the tip, split into three segments for the gradient. I'll import the glow kit and apply it directly to flat-colored parts. Now I'm positioning a small gold maker's mark emblem on the anvil's front face.

Still placing anvil decoration...

Adding U-shaped staples and nail spikes at the base plate edges to anchor it into the stump. For the palette, I'm settling on a limited set around six custom colors—steel highlights, scorch marks, dark holes, and a touch of mossy green on the stump for natural detail.

Now I'm working out the axe-gash coloring, using a deep near-black brown for the cut interior and a lighter pale wood tone for the exposed fresh chips, keeping to roughly six custom colors total. For the stump itself, I'm planning a dark bark cylinder body with alternating lighter bark ridges, and a paler heartwood tone for the cut top surface.

For the top of the stump, I'm placing a thin cut-wood disc slightly smaller than the trunk radius, sitting just above a 0.40-tall dark bark cylinder, with concentric growth rings rendered as thin rotated ring shapes facing upward at increasing radii, colored in the mid-tone wood shade. Now I'm adding root flares at the trunk's base for a more natural look, planning to use wedge-shaped forms angled outward in a radial pattern around the bottom of the trunk, considering simple tapered box or cone shapes to approximate the flared root silhouette.

I need to keep roots within the bounding box, checking that the z-extent stays under the 0.35 limit by adjusting the root start radius to 0.245 and profile length to 0.09. Now I'm adding texture details: thin vertical ridge boxes rotated to face outward, bark knots and gouges as dark small boxes, and axe marks as thick dark diagonal slashes positioned tangentially with rotation. I'm also placing axe gashes on the top cap near the edges, working out the angle-based positioning formula so each element rotates correctly to face outward from the trunk's center.

Confirming rotation uses degrees as documented. Now I'm working out the iron bands: two cylindrical bands near the base with slightly larger radius than the trunk to cover it, adding a thin highlight ring at the top edge of each for depth, and placing six rivets per band at the face centers of a 12-gon cross-section, sized and positioned just outside the band surface.

Still placing rivets and figuring band details...

Now I'm adding the cap geometry above the trunk — a flattened cylinder disc with bark rim ridges beneath, sized slightly wider than the trunk top so it overhangs, and adding a few radial crack details etched into the cap surface at different angles.

Then I'm working out the spark effects: small glowing cubes in hot yellow and ember tones, randomly rotated and positioned above the campfire bar within a bounded region, roughly 16 of them with added glow material and strength, plus some elongated streak-like sparks for variation.

Picking edge highlight colors...

Still working out the emblem placement...

Still writing frustum geometry...

Adding ridge color alternation, dark knot details at face centers, and axe-mark slashes carved into the trunk surface at angled intervals...

I'm sizing concentric rings positioned near the top of the anvil, checking their radii against the plate corners so they stay visible, and working out the rotation needed to make the ring geometry face upward correctly after transforming it from its default forward-facing orientation.

Mapping local scale to world axes after rotation, so vertical radius becomes 0.066 and depth radius 0.0975, placing the horn base at y=0.714 with the tip sloping down to 0.73. I'll create a helper function for placing parts under bones, and figure out how to give the skull a blocky, faceted look using low-segment geometry with scaling rather than a smooth sphere, positioning the face front and beard to drape naturally down the chest.

Working out the flat-face rotation math for the faceted cylinder head, I get the front face sitting at about z=0.057, so eyes should go near y=1.24, z=0.05. Then I'm planning the jaw as a separate box/cylinder piece hinged near (0,1.15,-0.02), extending down to cover the lower face.

For the mouth and beard, I'm thinking a dark slit mouth mostly hidden by facial hair, with the beard's main mass attached partly to the jaw bone so it moves naturally when the jaw opens, even though a large beard there is a bit unusual rigging-wise.

For the neck joint, I'm adding a thick cylinder skin section around y 1.02-1.12 that stays mostly concealed under the beard, plus considering additional plating there.

Beyond the brow box itself, I'm layering in bushy eyebrow geometry using the hair color, plus small cones jutting from the outer ends for texture. I'm also tweaking the head's z-scale slightly to adjust how far forward the flat face sits, making sure the eyes and brow still land correctly on that facet.

I'm now fine-tuning the vertical placement of facial features: adjusting eye height to 1.225, brow center to 1.262 with bushy extension to 1.275, and repositioning the band to 1.30-1.34 so it clears the brows, with the head top at 1.35 and hair dome at 1.34.

Still writing details for the band's gold rivets positioned around its flat faces at evenly spaced angles, skipping the front face where the stud sits.

Still working out blade splay angles...

Now I'm planning the moustache as a handlebar shape with thick tapered sweeps curling outward and up from under the nose, using a curved path per side.

Next I'm placing the jaw itself as a skin-toned block beneath the beard, and adding a dark slit for the mouth between the moustache and lower beard to keep the layering readable.

Adding small white teeth peeking from the jaw under the moustache, then re-adjusting the vertical layout: upper skull cylinder spanning 1.11 to 1.35, eyes centered around 1.225, nose at 1.17, mouth at 1.125, and jaw positioned slightly below with a joint pivot near 1.15, accepting a bit of overlap with the skull.

Now working out per-side brow ridges and bushy brow geometry, adding small cone tufts at the outer and inner ends for texture, and deciding on a contrasting hair/beard color for the brows.

For the ears I'm placing flattened spheres with pointed cone tips on either side of the head, positioning them to align with the rotated flat facets of the head shape so they sit naturally against the skull.

Adding an earring and hair dome...

Adding gold temple discs and thin trim cylinders around the helmet band, keeping skip on fine ear tufts since they're minor details.

Now I'm working out facial feature placement — the mustache sweep, neck cylinder positioning near the jaw, and sizing the beard mass sphere so its front tip sits just past the chin without overshooting too far forward.

Working out blade positions and angles for one side, checking overlap with the jaw cylinder's front z-coordinate to confirm the blades sit correctly against the head geometry, then checking how the outer blade aligns with the jaw's octagonal cross-section.
